title: Maximum Subsequence Score
summary: Given two equal-length integer arrays nums1 and nums2, and a positive integer k, select a subsequence of indices from nums1 of length k.
statement: Given two equal-length integer arrays nums1 and nums2, and a positive integer k, select a subsequence of indices from nums1 of length k. The score is the sum of the selected elements from nums1 multiplied by the minimum of the corresponding selected elements from nums2. Find the maximum score possible.
constraints: Choose exactly k common indices from the equal-length arrays.
The score is the selected nums1 sum multiplied by the minimum selected nums2 value.
hints: Sort index pairs by nums2 from largest to smallest.
At each position, the current nums2 is the minimum for any selection formed from the processed prefix.
Maintain the k largest nums1 values in that prefix with a min-heap and track their sum.
For every possible selected minimum, the heap maximizes the accompanying sum; checking all thresholds therefore finds the global optimum.
editorial: For every possible selected minimum, the heap maximizes the accompanying sum; checking all thresholds therefore finds the global optimum.

tests.explanation: Choosing indices zero, two, and three gives sum six and minimum two, scoring twelve.
For one index, nums1[2] times nums2[2] gives the maximum score thirty.
